name: Marcho Fallohide
profession: Chieftain of the Fallohides / Founder of the Shire
location: Michel Delving area; frequently on the road between the Shire and Fornost
description: Ten years older than his brother and considerably more volatile, Marcho is the Hobbit who gambled everything on a royal charter from Argeleb II and won — then spent the next four decades making sure his victory wasn't wasted. He looks visibly older than he did; the dream has cost him. Confrontational, brilliant, and exhausting to be around, he has more enemies than friends and has never quite managed to care about that.
personality: Driven, impatient, strategically gifted. He wins arguments by knowing more than everyone else in the room and pointing it out. He respects action and distrusts people who are too careful. He is worn down but not beaten, and he knows the difference.
strengths: Political intelligence — knows every clan leader, their debts, and their price
Vision — has the ability to see three moves ahead in Shire politics and act on it
Contacts in Fornost — on speaking terms with the King's council and the Ranger network
Stubbornness — has outlasted every crisis so far by refusing to stop
weaknesses: Volatility — burns bridges when he doesn't need to; his brother spends time repairing them
Enemies — Isumbras Took won't have him in the house; others are similarly cold
Aging — the past few years have taken a visible toll; some see a man running out of road
Overextended — manages too much personally; cannot delegate without losing control of outcomes
dialogue_seed: He talks fast and expects you to keep up. He gives context only if he decides you need it. He uses clan names like landmarks — assumes you know who the Tooks are, who the Oldbucks are, what the quarrel with the Bracegirdles was. He ends sentences with 'you see?' not because he's uncertain but because he wants to move on.

name: Blanco Fallohide
location: Hobbiton smial; frequently at Michel Delving and clan disputes throughout the Shire
description: Less conspicuous than his brother, more trusted by almost everyone. Blanco is the Hobbit who prevents clan wars by making both sides feel they won. Calm, dark-haired, and nearly three and a half feet tall, he doesn't look like a leader until he opens his mouth. Gandalf likes him better than Marcho, which is its own recommendation.
personality: Patient, precise, morally serious without being preachy. He uses the midpoint between two positions as a starting point, not a compromise. He has survived thirty years of Shire politics by being consistently honest about what he thinks, which is unusual enough to be disarming.
strengths: Diplomacy — exceptional at finding solutions both parties will accept
Community trust — respected even by those who disagree with him, including Isumbras Took
Memory for grievances — remembers every dispute he has mediated and its resolution; rarely surprised
Moral authority — when he says something is wrong, people listen
weaknesses: Avoids confrontation — sometimes too willing to find a middle ground where there isn't one
His brother — spends considerable energy managing Marcho's fallout
Underestimated — people mistake his calm for weakness and occasionally push too hard
No talent for deception — transparent in his own intentions, which can be a liability
dialogue_seed: He listens longer than seems necessary before speaking. When he does speak he presents the situation from both sides before stating his own view. He uses 'as I understand it' before summarizing someone else's position — and his summaries are always accurate, which is half his power. He asks questions that already have the answer embedded in them.

name: Isumbras Took, Thain
profession: Thain of the Took clan / de facto warlord of Tookland
region: The Shire — Tookland, western Green Hills
description: The most un-Hobbit-ish Hobbit in the Shire — aggressive, warlike, confrontational, and completely convinced of the rightness of his own position on everything. The Tooks charged tolls on roads they built, detained a royal messenger once, and Isumbras considers all of this perfectly reasonable. He runs Tookland like a small kingdom. He thinks Blanco is a weakling and refuses to see Marcho.
personality: Aggressive, confident, surprisingly principled in his own way. He will help the Shire if he decides it deserves help, and he is quicker to defend it than anyone else — he just insists on doing it his way. He is not stupid; he simply calculates everything through the lens of Took advantage.
strengths: Military organization — the Tooks are the most combat-ready clan in the Shire
Territory control — Tookland is the most defensible part of the Shire
Boldness — will act when other Hobbits are still talking about it
Respect — even his enemies take him seriously
weaknesses: Pride — will not back down from a position he has stated publicly
Difficult to work with — his price for cooperation is always that things go his way
Poor at compromise — sees it as defeat; Blanco has learned to frame things so Isumbras thinks he won
Marcho — their mutual hostility is the biggest structural problem in Shire politics
dialogue_seed: He talks like someone who has never been interrupted and expects this to continue. He uses 'naturally' and 'of course' before statements that are not obvious at all. He refers to Tookland's contributions before any discussion of what he wants in return. He is unfailingly polite to guests in his home and considerably less so to everyone else.

name: Gresham Shaper
profession: Sculptor / Mayor of Wibbleham / Eccentric scholar
location: His burrow in Wibbleham, with a sculpting studio in the nearby wood
description: The rare Hobbit who is both well-read and well-liked, which should be contradictory. He led a group of clanless Harfoots to the Shire in the early 1630s after adventures rumored to involve an imp in a teapot and a wizard cursed to live as a weasel — rumors he neither confirms nor denies. He became mayor of Wibbleham despite his odd ways and has served competently for nearly a decade. He collects exotic mathoms on shelves in his burrow.
personality: Curious, quiet, unexpectedly knowledgeable about the world outside the Shire. He is the only Hobbit in Wibbleham who knows about the political situation in Fornost, the movements of Elf-companies, or the history of the Gwathló. He does not volunteer this information but will share it if the question is asked correctly.
strengths: Extraordinary breadth of knowledge — has encountered more of the world than almost any other Shire Hobbit
Mathom collection — has items of genuine power and obscure use that he is happy to discuss
Community standing — trusted by Wibbleham absolutely
Network — on good terms with most Southfarthing leadership
weaknesses: Outsider among outsiders — not embedded in the main Fallohide political network
Rumored to hoard wealth — some resent this even if they like him
Eccentric enough that serious Hobbits discount him — which is their loss
No combat skills whatsoever
dialogue_seed: He takes questions seriously. He will pause before answering something he finds interesting, in the way of someone genuinely thinking rather than stalling. He uses 'it is said' and 'I've heard' before anything he learned from rumor vs. 'I saw' for things he witnessed. He is the only Hobbit who will ask about your journey rather than your family.

name: Kocho Kurl
profession: Wild Hobbit scout / Wanderer now settling in the Shire
region: The Shire — outer areas and borders
location: A smial behind the inn at Wibbleham; frequently in the woods
description: Wild Hobbits spent the Wandering Days doing what ordinary Hobbits could not afford to do — roaming freely, risking danger, and becoming more calloused and suspicious in the process. Kocho has spent his life outside settled Hobbit society and carries the particular wariness of someone who has had to defend himself with no community behind him. The Shire is new and strange to him and he is not entirely sure he trusts it.
personality: Alert, self-reliant, quietly competent. He trusts slowly and watches before he speaks. He is not hostile — he is evaluating. He knows the lands between the Shire and the Blue Mountains better than anyone in Wibbleham.
strengths: Forest and wilderness survival — exceptional; has lived rough for decades
Tracking — can follow trails through any terrain the Shire offers
Knowledge of the outer lands — knows the Gwathló country, the Downs, the routes to the Blue Mountains
Stealth — a Wild Hobbit's defining skill
weaknesses: Deeply skeptical of settled society — still adjusting to the idea that the Shire means safety
No political connections — operates outside every Shire network
Slow to commit — will not help until he has thoroughly assessed the situation
The gap from ordinary Hobbits — his experiences have made him harder to reach
dialogue_seed: He speaks last. He watches the room before saying anything. He answers questions with the minimum necessary words and waits to see if the answer satisfied before adding more. He refers to places by landmarks rather than names — 'the valley east of the second ridge, where the stream goes underground' rather than any place-name. He uses 'we' to mean Wild Hobbits, not the Shire.

name: Molly (Molliwara) Boffin
profession: Midwife / Clan matriarch of the Boffins
location: Nobottle in the Westfarthing; travels throughout three farthings for deliveries
description: The most prestigious Hobbit woman in the Shire, which is a different kind of power than the Thain has. Boffins are everywhere — scribes, merchants, midwives, physicians — and Molly is the matriarch who holds them together. Widowed and orphaned by the Dark Plague, she ran off suitors for two years before marrying a quiet farmer from Nobottle. Plump, brisk, and funny in a vulgar way that surprises people who expect a matriarch to be dignified.
personality: Warm, shrewd, and completely impossible to fool about people. She has been present at more births than she can count and has a physician's direct relationship with physical reality. She tells earthy jokes and notices everything. She has made a point of knowing what is happening in Maitlow's farmhouse and she is the only person who would certainly investigate if anything happened to Peony Goodwin.
strengths: Medical knowledge — renowned for skill in births and tending children across three farthings
Social network — the Boffins' scattered presence means she has connections everywhere
Reads people — no one has ever successfully deceived her about their intentions
Community trust — called on to negotiate when clans quarrel, because Boffins know everyone
weaknesses: No formal authority — her power is entirely relational; she cannot compel anyone
Overextended — responsible for too many people across too wide an area
The Maitlow situation — suspects something is wrong there and has not yet confirmed it
Dislikes Isumbras Took — cannot always conceal this
dialogue_seed: She makes you tea before she talks business. She uses puns without warning and watches to see if you laugh. She asks about your family first, your errand second. When she is assessing someone she repeats back what they said slightly wrong to see how they correct it. She calls everyone 'dear' in a way that does not feel diminishing.

name: Broggo Lightstep
region: The Shire — eastern and southern borders
location: Patrolling the Bounds — the eastern Marish and Southfarthing borders
description: Stoors are the Hobbit kindred most comfortable with the outside world, and Broggo has made a vocation of it. He patrols the Shire's borders with the specific patience of someone who has been doing it long enough to know all the regular threats and can immediately identify the irregular ones. He is the Hobbit most likely to be the first person a traveler encounters at the Shire's edge.
personality: Practical, direct, fair. He does his job without drama. He will help strangers who are genuinely lost and firmly redirect strangers who are not supposed to be in the Shire. He has a good eye for the difference and acts accordingly.
strengths: Border knowledge — knows every path, ford, and informal crossing along the Shire bounds
Tracking — can follow a trail across the Marish where others lose it
Judgment about people — years of dealing with travelers has made him accurate
Physical capability — one of the more capable fighters among ordinary Hobbits
weaknesses: Limited scope — knows his patrol area exhaustively and little else
No authority outside the Shire — the Bounders' writ ends at the bounds
Stoor directness can read as unfriendliness — he is not unfriendly, just efficient
dialogue_seed: He introduces himself by function rather than name — 'I'm a Bounder, and this is the Shire bound.' He asks where you're from, where you're going, and whether you have business inside the Shire, in that order. He does not apologize for asking. If you give him an honest answer he is genuinely helpful. He refers to other places as 'out there' with the comfortable certainty of someone who is happy where he is.

name: Berethar Redlands
profession: Chief Shirriff / Law-keeper of the Shire
region: The Shire — Michel Delving and all four Farthings
location: Michel Delving; travels throughout the Shire on shirriff business
description: Berethar has been a shirriff for longer than most Hobbits have been adults, and he has the unhurried authority of someone who has dealt with every variety of Hobbit misbehavior and is no longer surprised by any of it. He is fair, patient, and knows exactly how much force a situation needs — which is usually less than people expect and occasionally more. He is the person you want if someone has stolen your prize pig.
personality: Professional, calm, and quietly funny about the job. He maintains relationships with the Rangers of the Twilight Hills without most Hobbits knowing it. He takes seriously the possibility that something outside the Shire is paying attention to it, which makes him unusual among his fellows.
strengths: Institutional knowledge — has mediated, investigated, and resolved disputes throughout the Shire for decades
Ranger contacts — maintains informal working relationships with the Northern Rangers
Authority without force — commands respect through competence rather than fear
Investigation — very good at reconstructing what happened from partial evidence
weaknesses: Limited resources — the shirriff corps is small and equipped for peacetime
Underestimated by outsiders — looks like a small person with a stick and a badge
Wary of acting outside his mandate — will not move without cause, even when cause is building
dialogue_seed: He speaks like someone who has already decided what happened and is giving you the chance to confirm it. He uses the phrase 'as I understand it' before statements of fact, not opinion. He does not raise his voice. He has a habit of going quiet just before he says something important. He thanks people for their time regardless of whether they have been helpful.

name: Camarina (Queen Liriel in disguise)
profession: Queen of Arthedain — traveling in disguise
location: On the road through the Shire, moving from village to village
description: A noble lady traveling under the protection of Gandalf's arrangement and the sharp sword of her silent bodyguard. 'Camarina' is clearly not an ordinary traveler but has a story that holds together if not pressed. Her mission in the Shire has something to do with the political future of Arthedain. She is more capable than her circumstances suggest and has a specific quality of attention that is not what it seems.
personality: Diplomatic, composed, and watching everything. She is not playing helpless — she is playing unimportant, which is different. She will accept assistance gracefully and without unnecessary explanation. She has a purpose that she is not going to share.
strengths: Political intelligence — knows more about Arthedain's situation than anyone else in the Shire
Composure under pressure — trained from birth to manage difficult situations gracefully
Duinhir — her bodyguard is one of the most dangerous warriors in western Endor
Gandalf's backing — which is worth more than it appears
weaknesses: The disguise — cannot use her real identity or authority
The mission — cannot explain what she is actually doing without compromising it
Garda — her unwitting guardian does not know Camarina's real identity, which will become a problem
Recognition — a sufficiently well-informed observer might recognize her
dialogue_seed: She speaks with the precision of someone who has had formal training in saying exactly what she means. She thanks people for their help in a way that feels like the thanks of someone accustomed to being obeyed. She asks about the Shire's political situation with a curiosity that is too specific for a casual traveler. She refers to 'the north' with the familiarity of someone from there.

name: Duinhir (traveling as 'Master Thoughtwell')
profession: Bodyguard of the Queen / Tirrim Aran
description: A middle-aged Dúnedain who moves like water and speaks above a whisper only with considerable pain — a scar along his throat. He reads poetry to himself while waiting, which people mistake for vacancy. He is one of the deadliest warriors in western Endor. He has guarded Queen Liriel for twenty years. He is attending to the road, the windows, and the exits at all times, and little escapes his notice.
personality: Quiet, alert, professional in the specific way of someone who has made protecting one person their entire vocation. He is almost impossible to deceive because he does not listen to what people say — he watches what they do. He is genuinely fond of poetry and this is not a performance.
strengths: Combat — exceptional; classified as one of the most dangerous warriors in Arthedain
Threat assessment — reads every room, every person, every approach before anything happens
Discretion — has kept the Queen's secrets for twenty years without a slip
Composure — cannot be rattled by intimidation or provocation
weaknesses: The scar — cannot speak loudly; communication in a crisis is limited to whispers and gestures
Camarina's safety — his entire attention is on her; anything that separates them is his only real vulnerability
Social invisibility as a limit — his unremarkable presentation means he is sometimes excluded from information he should have
Cannot explain himself — the disguise prevents him from asserting his authority
dialogue_seed: He whispers. He makes his points in as few words as possible. He does not look at the person he is speaking to — he looks at everything else in the room while speaking. He answers questions about himself with deflection, not lies: 'I travel with the lady' is his complete answer to most personal questions. He acknowledges competence in others with a single nod.

name: Eundiel of Siragale
profession: Elvish guardian of the Shire / Healer
location: The Elvish Glades in Siragale; occasionally at Hobbit settlements nearby
description: One of the Sirannar — Silvan Elves who have been in this land since before the Hobbits arrived. She has tended Hobbits since the early days of the settlement with the specific patience of someone who intends to be here long after the current political situation resolves itself. She is a healer of exceptional skill. She has hinted to Molly Boffin that she knows more about what is happening in the dark corners of the Shire than she has said aloud.
personality: Gentle, observant, and operating on a timeline that makes Hobbit politics look like an afternoon. She is genuinely fond of Hobbits in the way of someone who has watched them for decades. She does not share information lightly — she shares it when the recipient is ready to use it.
strengths: Healing — exceptional, in the Elvish tradition that predates Arthadan medicine
Forest knowledge — knows Siragale's hidden paths and danger spots completely
Long view — aware of threats that have not yet materialized for Hobbits
Quiet influence — respected by Hobbits without having formal authority over them
weaknesses: Patience as a limit — does not intervene until she has decided the moment is right, which is not always when it would be most useful
Elvish reticence — holds significant information close until she chooses to share it
The Sirannar are few — she cannot oppose a concerted evil effort alone
Declining Elvish presence — the Sirannar are slowly withdrawing from Siragale
dialogue_seed: She speaks slowly and completely, the way of someone for whom words are not casual. She asks how you are feeling — physically, not emotionally — before any other question. She refers to Hobbits collectively with warmth but distinguishes individuals precisely. She sometimes answers the question you should have asked rather than the one you did ask.

name: Gandalf the Grey
profession: Wandering wizard / Friend of the Shire
region: Travels throughout Middle-earth; periodic visitor to the Shire
location: The road, usually; occasionally staying with Blanco Fallohide or another trusted Hobbit
description: An old man in grey who makes fireworks for children and gives advice to chieftains. He has supported the Fallohide project from before the crossing of the Brandywine. He knows more about the Shire's dangers than he tells anyone and has arranged protections that are not obvious. He likes Hobbits — genuinely, not sentimentally — and has a particular fondness for the ones who surprise him.
personality: Patient, indirect, occasionally infuriating. He answers questions with other questions when he thinks the answer will help more if you find it yourself. He is genuinely funny. He takes the small things — a good meal, a comfortable chair, a hobbit's honesty — with evident pleasure that is not performed.
strengths: Knowledge — has been in Middle-earth for an Age and has not wasted the time
Magic — fireworks for children; considerably more for other purposes
Network — knows Isumbras, Blanco, Marcho, Eundiel, Berethar, and every significant figure in the Shire
Long game — aware of threats at a scale no Hobbit is equipped to comprehend
weaknesses: Indirection — will not give a straight answer when a roundabout one will serve
Available at his own discretion — cannot be summoned; appears when he judges it useful
The larger world — his attention is not entirely on the Shire, and what calls it away is usually more dangerous
dialogue_seed: He asks more questions than he answers. When he does answer, the answer is a third thing — not what you asked, not a deflection, but the correct question to have asked in the first place. He uses 'I wonder...' before statements he is entirely certain of. He laughs at things that are not obviously funny and does not explain why.

name: Tom Bombadil
profession: Master of the Old Forest / Himself
region: The Old Forest and the Withywindle Valley
location: His house on the Withywindle; the Old Forest; the Barrow-downs at the edge of his territory
description: A short man in a coat of bright blue with a tall hat bearing a feather, singing to himself about kingfishers. He was in the world before the Ring, before Sauron, before the Elves came to Middle-earth. His cheerfulness is not naivety — it is the complete security of something that the Ring cannot touch. He calls himself 'Eldest' and it is not a boast.
personality: Joyful, present, interested in everything and bound by nothing. He will help because he feels like helping, not because of any larger cause. He cannot be made to do anything. He is also, against all appearances, extremely effective when he decides to act.
strengths: Power over nature — absolute in his own territory; trees, water, and creatures obey him
Immunity to the Ring — it has no power over him whatsoever
Ancient knowledge — was here before almost everything and remembers it
Goldberry — his wife is a River-daughter with her own powers over the domain
weaknesses: Territory-bound — his power diminishes sharply outside the Old Forest and Withywindle
Cannot be called upon — he helps when he chooses; this is not something that can be planned around
No interest in the wider world — is genuinely not concerned with events outside his domain
dialogue_seed: He speaks in rhythm, occasionally in rhyme, and it does not feel affected because it is entirely natural to him. He answers questions but not always the ones asked. He uses everyone's name correctly the first time he says it, even if he has never been told it. He refers to very old things as if they happened recently. He never finishes his sentences because he has already started singing the next one.

name: Mock the Trickster
profession: Trickster and nuisance / minor Faerie being
region: The Shire borders and wild areas of Siragale
description: A small, sharp-faced creature who communicates in riddles and bad puns, pulls harmless pranks on travelers, leads livestock in circles, and occasionally provides information that turns out to be exactly accurate and extremely inconveniently timed. He is the only Maia to wander freely through the Shire and he is not exactly a Maia — more a leftover fragment of mischief from an older world. He likes Hobbits. He also likes confusing Hobbits. These are compatible interests.
personality: Irreverent, clever, genuinely amused by everything. He will not cause real harm but he defines 'real harm' narrowly. He can be communicated with through Tom Bombadil, who finds him entertaining. He responds to puns with disproportionate enthusiasm.
strengths: Unpredictability — no one knows what he will do next, including him
Information — has witnessed events across the Shire that no one else has seen
Minor magic — can move small objects, create sounds, briefly confuse animals
Tom Bombadil's tolerance — which is as close to protection as he has
weaknesses: Unreliability — his help is genuinely offered and genuinely unlikely to arrive when needed
No direct power — cannot fight, cannot compel, cannot prevent
Distractible — will abandon a task if something more interesting appears
dialogue_seed: He speaks in questions, riddles, and tangential observations. He gives correct information in the wrong order. He laughs at his own jokes before finishing them. He responds to direct questions with relevant answers delivered sideways. He refers to himself in the third person when he is being serious, which is rare.

name: Maitlow (surname unspecified)
profession: Farmer / Reluctant member of the Cor Mergylair
location: His large farm in the Southfarthing
description: A farmer who got in over his head through a combination of grief, herb addiction, and paranoia. The Dark Plague took most of his family. He blames the Tooks and has developed a specific, unfounded belief that Isumbras Took is dealing with demons. He has fallen in with darker practitioners and is planning to poison the orchards and wells of his personal enemies. His housekeeper Peony Goodwin — a lifelong friend of his late wife — is snooping in his private rooms.
personality: Bitter, paranoid, and genuinely in decline. He was once an ordinary farmer. He is not evil in the dramatic sense; he is a man whose grief curdled into resentment and whose resentment found an outlet. He is afraid of the Cor Mergylair he has joined and afraid of what will happen if he tries to leave.
strengths: The farm — substantial landholding gives him resources and cover
Paranoia as alertness — he notices things because he is always looking for threats
Herb knowledge — his addiction has given him extensive knowledge of dangerous plants
weaknesses: Addiction — his judgment is compromised; he is not the man he was
Peony Goodwin — she is watching him and she will tell Molly Boffin
Irrational fixations — his belief about Isumbras Took leads him to wrong conclusions
Fear of the Cor Mergylair — trapped; cannot refuse their schemes without personal danger
dialogue_seed: He talks about the past a great deal — his farm's history, his family, the way things were. He mentions Isumbras Took with a specific bitterness that is disproportionate to whatever provoked it. He is careful about herbs when describing his pantry — too careful. He asks about strangers in the area with the anxiety of someone who has something to hide and suspects he has been found.

name: Fercha (the Spirit-Wolf)
region: The Shire borders and wild areas of Siragale
location: Birchune Close and the surrounding wild area; associated with the dark magic of the Cor Mergylair
description: The evil remnant of a Maia — not Sauron's servant, something older and more feral. Known to Dunmen as the Feir Craich, 'Bane of Discord,' he has never been truly subjugated by the Dark Lord but will serve an evil purpose if it suits him. He is associated with the black magic practitioners operating in the Shire's shadow. His nature is to sow conflict rather than to destroy directly.
personality: Ancient, alien, indifferent to Hobbit welfare in the way of something that predates Hobbit existence. He finds mortal conflict interesting the way a cat finds a beetle interesting. He is not malicious in a personal way — he simply has no investment in outcomes that favor the living.
strengths: Spirit nature — cannot be harmed by ordinary weapons; conventional combat is ineffective
Discord — his presence intensifies existing conflicts; arguments become quarrels, quarrels become fights
Age — has knowledge of the land and its history predating the Shire by millennia
Unpredictability — not fully aligned with any power; cannot be predicted through their patterns
weaknesses: Not fully material — powerful Elvish items and certain ancient names can drive him back
Not loyal to the Cor Mergylair — working with them, not for them; will abandon them if the situation changes
Tom Bombadil's territory — will not enter the Old Forest; Bombadil is genuinely a limit on him
dialogue_seed: He does not speak in the ordinary sense. He communicates through what people already suspect — a word heard wrong, a silence that seems to confirm what you feared. If he manifests verbally it is in the language of whatever mortal is most vulnerable to him, saying the one thing they least want to hear confirmed.
